subject: Next steps: HIPAA/BAA scope, PHI boundaries, and QSA timeline
messages:
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Stevens <alex.stevens@luminacare.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 03 Aug 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Recap + immediate asks: HIPAA / BAA scope and PHI handling

Alex — thanks again for the conversation today. Quick recap and proposed next steps to make sure we align on compliance needs and timelines: 

Summary:
- You confirmed LuminaCare will be evaluating Redwood to power PHI-containing workflows for a pilot (clinical notes ingestion + summarization).
- Primary concerns: BAA availability, whether PHI can be processed on our hosted offering, and what deployment modes are eligible.

Quick answers (high level):
- BAA: We can execute a BAA for dedicated and private deployments. For hosted multi-tenant API we generally require an enterprise contract and additional controls; we usually recommend Dedicated or Private for PHI.
- PHI handling boundaries: PHI may be processed when the customer uses Dedicated (isolated GPU pools) or Private (VPC/on-prem) with customer-managed keys. Shared hosted endpoints are not recommended for PHI without contractual exceptions.
- Artifacts: I attached our SOC 2 summary (recent) and noted the vendor security questionnaire you mentioned.

Immediate next steps I propose:
1) You share the vendor security questionnaire (attached to your reply) — Ben (CC'd) will triage and start answering.
2) Marissa will schedule a short compliance call with our Solutions Architect to review encryption, KMS, audit logs, and data retention options.
3) We’ll outline a target timeline to get a signed BAA and pilot start date (I suggest 3–4 weeks assuming questionnaire Q/A goes smoothly).

Can you confirm the preferred deployment option (Dedicated vs Private) and whether you need the endpoint in us-west-2? That will help us provide a concrete timeline.

Thanks — I’ll wait for the questionnaire and any priority items.

—Rachel
Rachel Kim
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference

From: Alex Stevens <alex.stevens@luminacare.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: LuminaCare Security Team <security@luminacare.com>
Date: Mon, 03 Aug 2026 16:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Recap + immediate asks: HIPAA / BAA scope and PHI handling

Thanks Rachel — this is helpful. Attaching our vendor security questionnaire (VSA-2026_LuminaCare.pdf). A few clarifications up-front:

- Preferred deployment: Dedicated in us-west-2 if we can get guaranteed isolation and audit logs. If Dedicated timeline is long, we are open to Private (VPC) but prefer Redwood-managed infra if contractually possible.
- Timeline: pilot target is Sept 20 (tight) — we need BAA and questionnaire complete beforehand.
- Some items to flag from our side: data retention options for KV cache and any pre-tokenization handling of PHI (we'd like assurances that PII/PHI is not persisted beyond configured retention windows).

We'll await the SOC 2 summary and answers to the questionnaire. If you can set up the compliance call this week, that would be great.

Alex
Alex Stevens
Head of Integrations — LuminaCare
alex.stevens@luminacare.com
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 04 Aug 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap + immediate asks: HIPAA / BAA scope and PHI handling

Rachel — thanks for the heads-up and the questionnaire. I started a pass on the VSA PDF (attached to my internal notes). Notes and actions: 

- SOC 2: our latest Type II report (redacted) is ready; I attached the SOC2-summary.pdf we send to prospects (controls, scope, and last audit period).
- BAA: Legal prefers to route BAAs for Dedicated/Private. For hosted we can provide a BAA but it requires Enterprise contract amendments and scoping (specifically around encryption at rest and shared model caching).
- PHI handling: recommended approach for LuminaCare pilot is Dedicated with KV cache disabled for persistence and strict retention (30 days or configurable). Private (VPC) can give them customer-managed KMS and full audit logs if they insist on that level.

Proposed internal owners:
- I’ll own the questionnaire responses (security controls, encryption, incident response).
- Marissa can book the compliance call and bring Solutions Architecture to review logs/KMS/retention settings.

Risk/unknowns to surface to LuminaCare on the compliance call:
- If they use redaction/pre-tokenization client-side vs server-side — if server-side, we need explicit acceptance in the BAA around transient PHI processing.
- Any requirement for delegated penetration testing or QSA involvement may add 2+ weeks.

I’ll draft answers by end of day tomorrow so we can share before the call.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Security & Privacy Programs
Redwood Inference
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Stevens <alex.stevens@luminacare.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 05 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap + immediate asks: HIPAA / BAA scope and PHI handling

Alex — appreciate the rapid turnaround and the questionnaire. Short plan and asks from our side so you have visibility before the compliance call: 

Planned deliverables before the call:
- Ben will send a completed vendor questionnaire response (we expect to return the first-pass answers within 48 hours).
- I attached our SOC 2 summary to this thread (Redwood_SOC2-summary.pdf).
- Marissa will send calendar invites for a 45-minute compliance deep dive (please include any members of your security/compliance team).

Key questions for the call (so we can head off long threads):
1) Do you expect client-side PHI redaction or will you send raw PHI to our endpoints? If client-side, we can focus on secure transit and storage options; if server-side, the BAA will need explicit language about transient processing and retention policies.
2) Confirm target retention window for prompt history / KV cache and whether you require immutable audit logs for every token processing event.
3) Any vendor risk items that require third-party attestations (e.g., penetration test results, FedRAMP-adjacent controls)?

Proposed timeline (tentative):
- 48–72h: vendor questionnaire first pass and SOC2 material shared.
- 1 week: compliance call and any follow-up clarifications.
- 2–4 weeks: finalize BAA and contract amendments (depends on counterparty legal load).

If Sept 20 is the pilot start target, we should plan to lock down the BAA and deployment selection by mid-August. Let me know if LuminaCare needs a redlineable BAA template in advance — I can have Legal send it to you.

Thanks — will coordinate invites.

—Rachel
